1169: | Magic Byte | Frame Len  | Sequence Byte | Payload ID    | Timestamp (Ticks)  | Raw Payload | Checksum      |
1170: | 0x55 (1B)  | uint8 (1B) | uint8 (1B)    | uint16_le(2B) | uint32_le (4B)     | (Len-10 B)  | CRC16 / CRC32 |
1171: +------------+------------+---------------+---------------+--------------------+-------------+---------------+
1172: ```
1173: 
1174: | Field Name | Offset | Type | Description |
1175: |---|---|---|---|
1176: | `Magic` | `0x00` | `uint8` | Always `0x55` (`85`). Synchronizes frame boundaries. |
1177: | `Length` | `0x01` | `uint8` | Total length of the frame including header, payload, and checksum ($10 \le \text{Length} \le 255$). |
1178: | `Sequence` | `0x02` | `uint8` | Sequence counter or sub-header flag. |
1179: | `Payload ID` | `0x03 - 0x04` | `uint16_le` | Unique numerical identifier of the sensor telemetry struct. |
1180: | `Timestamp` | `0x05 - 0x08` | `uint32_le` | Hardware clock counter (microsecond ticks since flight controller boot). |
1181: | `Payload Data`| `0x09` | `uint8[Len - 10 - ChecksumLen]` | Binary struct matching `Payload ID`. |
1182: | `Checksum` | End of frame | `uint16_le` or `uint32_le` | Frame integrity verification checksum. |
1183: 
1184: ### 6.3 Checksum Algorithms (CRC16-CCITT & CRC32)
1185: 
1186: 1. **Standard Sensor Frames (CRC16-CCITT)**:
1187:    - Polynomial: $x^{16} + x^{12} + x^5 + 1$ (`0x1021`), Initial value: `0x3692` or `0xFFFF`.
1188:    - Computed over all bytes from `Magic` through the last byte of `Payload Data`.
1189: 2. **Extended Multi-Sector Frames (CRC32)**:
1190:    - Standard IEEE 802.3 CRC32 (Polynomial: `0xEDB88320`).
1191: 
1192: ### 6.4 Sensor Telemetry Payload Definitions
1193: 
1194: | Payload ID (Hex) | Payload ID (Dec) | Sensor System | Core Fields Captured |
1195: |---|---|---|---|
1196: | `0x01` | `1` | `OSD / IMU Attitude` | Quaternions ($q_0, q_1, q_2, q_3$), 3-axis gyro rates (rad/s), 3-axis body accelerations ($m/s^2$), NED velocity ($v_x, v_y, v_z$). |
1197: | `0x02` | `2` | `GPS Raw` | Raw NMEA/UBX binary sentences: latitude, longitude, ellipsoidal altitude, horizontal/vertical accuracy, PDOP/HDOP, satellite PRN mask. |
1198: | `0x0A` | `10` | `Smart Battery` | Total battery voltage, discharge current draw ($mA$), pack temperature, individual cell voltages ($mV$), cell internal resistance ($m\Omega$). |
1199: | `0x12` | `18` | `Motor & ESC` | Real-time rotor RPM for motors 1 through 8, ESC input bus voltage, ESC current draw, ESC MOSFET power stage temperature (°C). |
1200: | `0x2A` | `42` | `Barometer & Compass` | Unfiltered atmospheric pressure (Pascals), calibrated barometric height ($m$), 3-axis magnetometer field strength ($mG$). |
1201: 
1202: ### 6.5 Log Cross-Referencing & Time Synchronization
1203: 
1204: To synchronize a 10 Hz mobile `.txt` log with a 100 Hz aircraft `.DAT` blackbox log:
1205: 
1206: 1. Extract `HomeDataRecorderFileIndex` from `.txt` Home Record (ID 2). Locate matching `FLY{index}.DAT`.
1207: 2. Locate the motor start event in `.txt` (`OsdFlyTime > 0` and `OsdIsMotorUp == 1`).
1208: 3. In `.DAT`, scan Payload `0x12` (Motor) for the timestamp where rotor RPM transitions from 0 to idle speed (> 1,200 RPM).
1209: 4. Compute the master synchronization offset:
1210:    $$\Delta t = t_{\text{DAT, motor\_start}} - t_{\text{TXT, motor\_start}}$$

### 5.8 Center Battery Telemetry (`CenterBatteryFlightRecordDataType`, ID 7)

Primary smart battery telemetry packet, broadcast at 2 Hz.

In DJI flight records, Record Type 7 encompasses **two distinct structural payload variants** depending on the log version, feature point (`FeaturePoint.FR_Standardization_Feature_Base_1` vs. `FeaturePoint.FR_Standardization_Feature_Battery_13`), and aircraft firmware generation. Decoders must not conflate these two layouts into a single monolithic schema.

#### 5.8.1 Variant A: Energy Summary Variant

Used in standard flight logs and base telemetry streams (`FeaturePoint.FR_Standardization_Feature_Base_1`; `ClsDjiLog.cs` lines 2773, 5902). This variant provides overall battery state-of-charge, total pack operational voltage, and aggregate energy capacities in milliampere-hours (mAh):

| Byte Offset | Type | Field Name | Unit / Scale Factor | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | `uint8` | `RelativeCapacity` | Percent (%) | Instantaneous State of Charge (SOC: $0 \dots 100\%$). |
| `1 - 2` | `uint16_le` | `CurrentPV` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Total battery pack real-time operational voltage ($V$). |
| `3 - 4` | `uint16_le` | `CurrentCapacity` | mAh | Instantaneous remaining battery energy capacity (`ReadInt(array[3], array[4])`). |
| `5 - 6` | `uint16_le` | `FullCapacity` | mAh | Total capacity when fully charged at current battery health (`ReadInt(array[5], array[6])`). |
| `7` | `uint8` | `BatteryCellCount` | Integer | Active number of cells in battery pack ($2 \dots 14$). |
| `8 - 9` | `int16_le` | `BatteryTemperature` | °C: $(\text{val} \div 10.0) - 273.15$ | Pack temperature sensor reading (converts raw deci-Kelvin to Celsius). |

#### 5.8.2 Variant B: Raw Cell Voltage Array Variant

Used in cell-level diagnostics and advanced telemetry logs (`FeaturePoint.FR_Standardization_Feature_Battery_13`; `ClsDjiLog.cs` lines 15720, 16685, 19874, 20850). In this variant, individual cell voltages are packed consecutively starting directly at byte offset `3 + num32`:

$$\text{CellVoltageOffset}(k) = (3 + num32) + 2 \times (k - 1) \quad \text{for cell } k \in [1 \dots 14]$$
$$\text{CellVoltage}_k = \frac{\text{ReadInt}(\text{array}[\text{offset}], \text{array}[\text{offset}+1])}{1000.0} \quad \text{(Volts)}$$

Where $num32 \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$ represents the dynamic sub-header / flag alignment offset ($num32 = 0$ for direct 0-indexed alignment, $num32 = 1$ when preceded by a 1-byte cell status prefix, or $num32 = -1$ on legacy compact layouts):

| Byte Offset ($num32 = 0$) | Type | Field Name | Unit / Scale Factor | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | `uint8` | `RelativeCapacity` | Percent (%) | Instantaneous State of Charge (SOC: $0 \dots 100\%$). |
| `1 - 2` | `uint16_le` | `CurrentPV` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Total battery pack real-time operational voltage ($V$). |
| `3 - 4` | `uint16_le` | `CellVoltage1` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cell 1 individual voltage ($mV \div 1000.0$). Offset: `3 + num32`. |
| `5 - 6` | `uint16_le` | `CellVoltage2` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cell 2 individual voltage ($mV \div 1000.0$). Offset: `5 + num32`. |
| `7 - 8` | `uint16_le` | `CellVoltage3` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cell 3 individual voltage ($mV \div 1000.0$). Offset: `7 + num32`. |
| `9 - 10` | `uint16_le` | `CellVoltage4` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cell 4 individual voltage ($mV \div 1000.0$). Offset: `9 + num32`. |
| `11 - 12` | `uint16_le` | `CellVoltage5` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cell 5 individual voltage ($mV \div 1000.0$, Enterprise / Agras). Offset: `11 + num32`. |
| `13 - 14` | `uint16_le` | `CellVoltage6` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cell 6 individual voltage ($mV \div 1000.0$, Enterprise / Agras). Offset: `13 + num32`. |
| `15 - 30` | `uint16_le[8]` | `CellVoltage7..14` | Volts $\div 1000.0$ | Cells 7 through 14 individual voltages (Heavy Enterprise / Agras T-series). |
| `31 + num32` | `uint8` | `BatteryCellCount` | Integer | Active number of cells in pack ($2 \dots 14$). |
| `32 + num32 .. 33 + num32` | `int16_le` | `BatteryTemperature` | °C: $(\text{val} \div 10.0) - 273.15$ | Pack temperature sensor reading (converts raw deci-Kelvin to Celsius). |

> ⚠️ **Critical Implementation Hazard — Cell Voltage Index Misalignment**:  
> Conflating Variant A and Variant B into a single record (i.e. assuming bytes 3–4 are `CurrentCapacity`, bytes 5–6 are `FullCapacity`, and cell voltages begin at byte 7) produces a severe **4-byte (2-cell) misalignment** when parsing raw cell voltage packets. On a standard 4S drone (e.g. Phantom or Mavic series), a decoder making this error will:
> - Read `CellVoltage3` as `CellVoltage1`.
> - Read `CellVoltage4` as `CellVoltage2`.
> - Read trailing pack metadata or zeroes as `CellVoltage3` and `CellVoltage4`.
> - Completely discard the true voltages of cells 1 and 2.
>
> Decoders must inspect the payload size and log `FeaturePoint` context: when decoding cell-level telemetry, individual cell voltages begin directly at byte offset `3 + num32` ($mV \div 1000.0$).

Present on dual-battery aircraft (Inspire 2, Matrice 200, Matrice 300 RTK, Matrice 350 RTK).  
Contains identical structural variants to `CenterBatteryFlightRecordDataType` (Variant A for energy summaries, Variant B for individual cell voltage arrays starting at `3 + num32`), mapping to `CenterBattery2Voltage1..14` and `CenterBattery2Temperature`.

#### 5.38.1 RTK Satellite Count Bitmask & Validity Logic (`GetRtkSatelliteCount`)

In DJI RTK telemetry packets, satellite count fields are **not** raw integer counts. Instead, each satellite count byte encodes a validity flag in Bit 0 and the actual satellite count in Bits 1–7.

The exact decoding logic implemented in `ClsDjiLog.cs` line 28800 is:

```csharp
private int GetRtkSatelliteCount(byte rawValue)
{
    if ((rawValue & 1) == 0)
    {
        return -999; // Constellation disabled, unequipped, or tracking unacquired
    }
    return rawValue >> 1; // True locked satellite count
}
```

Mathematically:
$$\text{Valid} = (\text{rawValue} \ \& \ 1) == 1$$
$$\text{SatelliteCount} = \begin{cases} \text{rawValue} \gg 1 & \text{if } (\text{rawValue} \ \& \ 1) == 1 \quad (\text{Valid Tracking}) \\ -999 & \text{if } (\text{rawValue} \ \& \ 1) == 0 \quad (\text{Invalid / Unequipped / Disabled}) \end{cases}$$

For example, a raw byte `0x1D` (`29` in decimal) represents 14 locked satellites ($29 \gg 1 = 14$), but naive interpretation reads 29 satellites—a +107% inflation error.
> 2. **Loss of Invalid / Unequipped Status**: When a GNSS constellation is disabled or unequipped (such as Galileo or QZSS on older D-RTK 2 base stations), the firmware emits `0x00`. Every message frame in a `.DAT` file adheres to a standardized framing structure:

```
+------------+------------+---------------+---------------+--------------------+--------------------------------+---------------+
| Magic Byte | Frame Len  | Sequence Byte | Payload ID    | Timestamp (Ticks)  | Raw Payload                    | Checksum      |
| 0x55 (1B)  | uint8 (1B) | uint8 (1B)    | uint16_le(2B) | uint32_le (4B)     | uint8[Len - 9 - ChecksumLen]   | CRC16 / CRC32 |
+------------+------------+---------------+---------------+--------------------+--------------------------------+---------------+
|<----------------------- 9-Byte Header (Offsets 0x00..0x08) ----------------->|<--- (Len - 9 - ChecksumLen B) ->|<- 2B or 4B -->|
```

| Field Name | Offset | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Magic` | `0x00` | `uint8` | Always `0x55` (`85`). Synchronizes frame boundaries. |
| `Length` | `0x01` | `uint8` | Total length of the frame including header, payload, and checksum ($11 \le \text{Length} \le 255$). Minimum physical frame length is 11 bytes with empty payload and 2-byte CRC16 (or 13 bytes for 4-byte CRC32). |
| `Sequence` | `0x02` | `uint8` | Sequence counter or sub-header flag. |
| `Payload ID` | `0x03 - 0x04` | `uint16_le` | Unique numerical identifier of the sensor telemetry struct. |
| `Timestamp` | `0x05 - 0x08` | `uint32_le` | Hardware clock counter (microsecond ticks since flight controller boot). |
| `Payload Data`| `0x09` | `uint8[Len - 9 - ChecksumLen]` | Binary struct matching `Payload ID`. Header spans exactly 9 bytes (`0x00`..`0x08`); payload starts at offset `0x09`. |
| `Checksum` | End of frame | `uint16_le` or `uint32_le` | Frame integrity verification checksum (CRC16-CCITT: 2 bytes, or CRC32: 4 bytes). |

#### 6.2.1 Header Size & Payload Boundary Derivation

Summing the individual header field sizes demonstrates that the frame header occupies exactly 9 bytes:
$$\text{HeaderSize} = \text{Magic}\,(1\,\text{B}) + \text{Length}\,(1\,\text{B}) + \text{Sequence}\,(1\,\text{B}) + \text{PayloadID}\,(2\,\text{B}) + \text{Timestamp}\,(4\,\text{B}) = 9\,\text{bytes}\quad (\text{offsets } 0x00 \dots 0x08)$$

Because the binary payload begins immediately at offset `0x09`, the payload data length is determined by subtracting the 9-byte header and the checksum length ($\text{ChecksumLen} \in \{2, 4\}$):
$$\text{PayloadLength} = \text{Length} - 9 - \text{ChecksumLen}$$

> ⚠️ **Implementation Warning — Off-by-One Framing & Allocation Hazard**:  
> Subtracting 10 bytes (such as `Len - 10 - ChecksumLen` or `Len - 10 B`) mistakenly treats the 9-byte header as 10 bytes, truncating the payload allocation by 1 byte and causing buffer under-reads or corruption of the final payload field.  
> Furthermore, with a 0-byte payload, the physical minimum frame length is:
> - **Standard CRC16 frames** ($\text{ChecksumLen} = 2$): $\text{Length}_{\min} = 9\,\text{(header)} + 0\,\text{(payload)} + 2\,\text{(CRC16)} = 11\,\text{bytes}$.
> - **Extended CRC32 frames** ($\text{ChecksumLen} = 4$): $\text{Length}_{\min} = 9\,\text{(header)} + 0\,\text{(payload)} + 4\,\text{(CRC32)} = 13\,\text{bytes}$.  
> The previous bound of 10 bytes ($10 \le \text{Length}$) is mathematically impossible for valid CRC-protected frames (yielding negative payload length $10 - 9 - 2 = -1$). Any frame with $\text{Length} < 11$ must be rejected as invalid stream noise.
